verdict.rationale: LaunchDarkly's own Environments feature spans development through production, and flag changes are tracked per environment. This gives a documented way to work in a non-production environment separate from production. The pack does not explicitly describe data isolation between environments or a sandbox an AI agent can be pointed at; 'Testing changes to flag targeting' appears only as a title with no content, so there is no dry-run evidence either. missing for 10: explicit documentation that non-production environments isolate production data, guidance on scoping AI agents (MCP/CLI/API tokens) to a sandbox environment, hands-on or independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: Environments allow you to manage your feature flags throughout your entire development lifecycle, from local development through production.
LaunchDarkly keeps a running log of changes made to feature flags and other resources in each environment.
set up and manage your feature flags, account members, projects, environments, teams, and other resources directly from the command line.
